rounds.text: Equilateral Enterprises Ltd is undergoing a dramatic, compounding acceleration in top-line growth that the market has completely failed to price in, sitting at just 15% of its 52-week range [E5]. Compounded sales growth has exploded across multiple timeframes, reaching 182% over 5 years [E15], 225% over 3 years [E16], and an astonishing 289% over the trailing twelve months [E17]. This stellar acceleration is further highlighted by a year-over-year sales surge of 49% [E58] and a multi-year sales uptrend [E61]. Crucially, this massive revenue expansion is translating into bottom-line delivery, evidenced by a 129% compounded profit growth over 3 years [E19] and a 33% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E20], comfortably beating the sector median profit growth of 21.8% [E68]. Furthermore, profit growth currently exceeds 1-year price growth by 67%, signaling that the company is starting to outperform expectations while the stock remains deeply compressed near its annual lows [E51]. On valuation, the stock trades at a very modest price-to-book ratio of 1.83x against a higher sector benchmark of 2.58x [E7], with the current share price at ₹ 16.6 against a book value of ₹ 9.08 [E2] for a micro-cap with a market capitalisation of ₹ 20.5 Cr [E3]. Conceded: [E1], [E4], [E6], [E14], [E18], [E63].

Equilateral Enterprises Ltd is currently undergoing a fundamental transformation, evidenced by a dramatic acceleration in sales growth from a 10-year average of 4% to a staggering 289% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E17]. This multi-year sales uptrend is supported by a 3-year compounded profit growth of 129%, which significantly outpaces the sector median profit growth of 21.8% [E16, E19, E68]. While the market currently prices the stock at a P/B of 1.83x, this represents a discount to the sector benchmark of 2.58x, suggesting the market has yet to fully account for the company's recent operational momentum [E2, E7]. The scanX signal engine confirms that the company is beginning to outperform expectations, with profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 67% [E51]. Conceded: the high P/E of 85.5x, the 0.00% dividend yield, and the fact that the stock is trading near the bottom of its 52-week range [E1, E4, E5]. Despite these headwinds, the company’s ability to sustain a 33% profit growth rate in the trailing twelve months highlights a clear shift in performance trajectory [E20].
